page: Microsoft Azure E96-24as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EASv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The server is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 28.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 1376 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing placing in the top 25%. PassMark memory scores also rank in the top 25%, reflecting high memory performance. However, multi-core CPU performance and most memory bandwidth tests fall into the average tier. For language model tasks, the server achieves strong text generation speeds of 298.02 tokens per second on small 135M models, but exhibits poor performance on large 70B models, processing only 4.97 tokens per second during prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server provides high memory density relative to its vCPU count, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads without paying for unnecessary compute cores. The primary tradeoff is the average multi-core scaling and poor performance on massive computational models. The hardware profile and benchmark results make this instance suitable for large in-memory databases, memory-heavy data processing, and enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM and local SSD storage.
